tier_evidence: Classic vasopressin-regulated exocytosis mobilizes a genuine apical-PM pool from storage vesicles (GLUT4-type mechanism), supported by five method observations.
Real recycling PM pool subject to dileucine-driven internalization, four method observations, two ec epitopes, and validated beta-secretase surface activity.
Reference case: dominantly Golgi/cytoplasmic but a minor, therapeutically targetable surface fraction in neuroendocrine tumor cells (basis of tarlatamab), five ec epitopes.
FcRn recycling/transcytosis surface pool (named RESCUE-type mechanism), a validated therapeutic target, with two ec epitopes despite intracellular-dominant steady state.
Validated cell-surface MHC-Ib and NK-checkpoint (NKG2A) ligand with a real universal surface pool and two ec epitopes despite ER-retained majority.
Kv10.2 shows constitutive genuine surface expression in overexpression systems (four observations); native surface is cell-cycle-gated, matching the OE-rescue pattern.
Cation-dependent mannose-6-phosphate receptor is a canonical recycling receptor cycling through the PM (~2.3% quantified) with one ec epitope, four observations.

Classic ligand-inducible ER-to-surface trafficking confirmed by live-cell flow across many cell types (11 OE observations) with ec_sites=2, making it a validated targetable surface pool on expression.
GPI-anchored surface co-receptor whose minority PM pool is confirmed by two independent direct methods (live-cell flow cytometry and functional surface assays) with a real ectodomain (ec_sites=3).

GLUT12 is a GLUT4-type insulin/AMPK/PKC-regulated transporter with a documented ~17% constitutive resting PM pool that expands on stimulation, a genuine regulated surface pool (ec_sites=0, delivery not display).

GLUT4 is the archetypal regulated-exocytosis transporter that reaches the PM as a functional pool expanding dramatically upon insulin/contraction (4 OE observations; ec_sites=0, delivery not display).
RANKL is the archetypal regulated-secretion ligand stored in secretory lysosomes and displayed at the surface upon mechanical/inflammatory activation; validated target (denosumab) with ec_sites=2.
